The `source` array references a tarball from the official npmjs.org registry, which is the expected upstream source for an npm package. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, indicating an intent to verify the integrity of the downloaded file, although this verification occurs later during `makepkg` execution, not during `--printsrcinfo`.

Importantly, there are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements at the global scope. The `package()` function is defined but will not be executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so its contents are out of scope for this safety gate. There is no evidence of malicious code execution, data exfiltration, or unsafe operations occurring during sourcing of this PKGBUILD.

Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD for `--printsrcinfo` is safe.

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It specifies the source of the package as the official NPM registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org/pele/-/pele-1.13.0.tgz`), which is the expected and legitimate source for this Node.js package. The `sha256sums` field contains a valid checksum for the tarball, indicating that the package maintainer intends to verify the integrity of the downloaded file—this is a secure practice.

There are no signs of malicious activity in this file. It does not execute code, perform network operations, or modify system settings. The file correctly declares dependencies (`nodejs>=20`), conflicts (`pele-git`), and other standard packaging metadata. The use of `noextract` is appropriate for prebuilt npm packages and does not pose a risk. All fields conform to standard AUR packaging practices.

While the source is a prebuilt JavaScript package from NPM (which is common but less transparent than building from source), this is not inherently malicious. The checksum is present and non-SKIP, which enhances trust in the artifact's integrity. No obfuscation, suspicious URLs, or dangerous commands are present.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR metadata with verified NPM source; no malicious content</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR metadata with verified NPM source; no malicious content
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Node.js package build process for "pele", a Mermaid renderer. It fetches a tarball from the official npm registry (https://registry.npmjs.org), which is an expected and trusted source for Node.js packages. The source integrity is verified using a SHA-256 checksum, which matches the published value. The package installation uses `bsdtar` to extract the npm package into the appropriate directory under `/usr/lib/node_modules`, a common pattern for Node.js utilities, and correctly installs the license file.

There are no signs of malicious behavior such as network exfiltration, obfuscated code, unauthorized file access, or execution of downloaded scripts. The build process is minimal and follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. The use of `noextract` with a compressed npm package and `--strip-components 1` is normal when extracting npm tgz files, as they typically include a top-level `package/` directory. All operations are confined to the package directory and follow expected conventions.

No dangerous commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, `wget`) are used, and no runtime or build-time network calls are made. The package depends only on `nodejs>=20`, which is necessary for the application to function. The metadata (URL, license, description) matches the upstream project on GitHub. There is no evidence of supply chain compromise or injected malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard Node.js package, no malicious code</summary>
</security_assessment>
